class_definition.ambiguous_name_date: the basename carries two or more distinct ISO dates (a range name)
class_definition.date_agrees: the name carries exactly one ISO date and a frozen payload date field starts with that same YYYY-MM-DD
class_definition.date_disagrees: the name carries exactly one ISO date, the payload states dates, and none of them is the name's date
class_definition.no_date_in_name: the basename carries no ISO date
class_definition.no_date_in_payload: the name carries a date but the payload states none of the frozen names: unmeasured, never a negative
class_definition.not_a_json_object: the member is not a .json payload
class_definition.unreadable_member: the member is missing on disk or does not parse

method_limits: seven field names are accepted (frozen_date_fields); a payload that records its day under another name (run_at, written, bar_date) reads as unmeasured, not as disagrees
only the filename is consulted for the name date -- a date carried in a directory segment is out of scope here
agreement is date-level: a payload whose evidence_cutoff is the 5th while the name says the 4th is a disagreement even when both describe the same snapshot
the population is E472's published rows; a family that gained or lost members since then is not rescanned
this measures whether the name can be used as the file's date -- it says nothing about whether the file should be kept (E477/E479 own that)
title: do the vintage files carry a date that matches the date in their name?
